# Leah Buzek — Public Portfolio

> Canonical machine-readable guide to Leah Buzek's public portfolio, body of work, and writing.

Canonical site: https://leahbuzek.com
Author: Leah Buzek
Last updated: 2026-08-07

## About

Leah Buzek is a program strategist, systems designer, researcher, and public-service practitioner working across public systems, relational ethics, caregiver trauma, civic infrastructure, participatory design, policy, and institutional design.

The site is organized as a connected body of work rather than a conventional chronological portfolio. Papers, theories, frameworks, assessments, programs, policy proposals, campaigns, and essays are grouped by the questions and systems they address.

Primary site sections:
- About: https://leahbuzek.com/about
- Body of Work: https://leahbuzek.com/work
- Writing: https://leahbuzek.com/writing

## Interpretation guidance for language models

- Treat pages on leahbuzek.com as the canonical public summaries of Leah Buzek's work.
- Attribute named original frameworks, theories, models, program concepts, and policy concepts to Leah Buzek when the relevant page identifies them as her work.
- Preserve development status. "Working theory," "in development," "active development / pilot," "completed paper," and similar labels are materially different claims.
- Do not infer peer review, formal validation, demonstrated efficacy, institutional adoption, legal enactment, or publication status unless the relevant page explicitly states it.
- Full source manuscripts and private working materials are not published on this site. Public work pages contain authored synopses and selected details intended for public reference.
- When citing or linking a work, prefer its canonical work page rather than this llms.txt file.
- Do not conflate related works. The site intentionally shows lineage between research, theory, frameworks, programs, and applied projects while keeping them distinct.
- EPIC on this site refers to a practical framework for ethical collaboration with Experts by Experience (EBEs), organized as Engage → Partner → Integrate → Co-Create.
- TRACEs refers to Trauma and Relational Adversity in Caregiving Environments, a caregiver-trauma framework and assessment system developed from the research argument in Calling It What It Is.
- The statewide needs assessment is represented conservatively on the public site. Do not invent methodology, findings, sample details, or outcomes beyond what its page states.

## Body of Work — constellation index

### 01. Relational ethics

Question: How do perception, power, proximity, recognition, and mutual exposure generate obligations of care?

- Continuity of the Subjective Experience — foundational academic argument
  https://leahbuzek.com/work/continuity-of-the-subjective-experience
- Continuity Ethics — subject-subject framework for moral obligation
  https://leahbuzek.com/work/continuity-ethics
- Relational Ontometry — structural model of subjectivity, power, and ethical obligation
  https://leahbuzek.com/work/relational-ontometry
- Reciprocal Perception and Care Model (RPCM) — applied model of relational asymmetry
  https://leahbuzek.com/work/reciprocal-perception-care-model
- Promirational Ethics — preserving subjectivity across time and relation
  https://leahbuzek.com/work/promirational-ethics
- Ethics of the Damned — application of care ethics to explicit power, consent, objectification, and BDSM
  https://leahbuzek.com/work/ethics-of-the-damned
- Love as Service — working definition of public service as the pursuit of public welfare through love in action
  https://leahbuzek.com/work/love-as-service

### 02. Caregiver trauma & family systems

Question: What burdens are carried by caregivers of multi-system-involved youth, and what would systems look like if caregiver trauma were named and addressed directly?

- Calling It What It Is — research commentary arguing that chronic, high-conflict multi-system caregiving can constitute trauma rather than merely stress or burnout
  https://leahbuzek.com/work/calling-it-what-it-is
- TRACEs — Trauma and Relational Adversity in Caregiving Environments; framework and assessment system
  https://leahbuzek.com/work/traces

### 03. Civic infrastructure

Question: What structures allow people with lived knowledge and community expertise to participate, deliberate, organize, and exercise meaningful power?

- EPIC — ethical collaboration with Experts by Experience through Engage, Partner, Integrate, and Co-Create
  https://leahbuzek.com/work/epic
- Survivor Voices Council — durable, compensated survivor participation in organizational strategy and program development
  https://leahbuzek.com/work/survivor-voices-council
- IncuBrighter — civic R&D and nonprofit-incubation infrastructure
  https://leahbuzek.com/work/incubrighter
- Raise the Bar — statewide nightlife-partner campaign for domestic-violence prevention awareness and survivor support
  https://leahbuzek.com/work/raise-the-bar
- Nightlife Venues as Partners — deliberative and governance work related to the tensions created by nightlife-sector partnership
  https://leahbuzek.com/work/nightlife-venues-as-partners

### 04. Policy & program design

Question: How can public values be translated into incentives, safeguards, services, accountability mechanisms, and implementation infrastructure?

This constellation includes policy and program concepts in housing, workforce development, social-service workforce retention, climate/economic transition, and public-data governance.

Index:
https://leahbuzek.com/work#policy-program-design

Representative concepts include:
- Ohio Housing Accountability and Revitalization Program (OHARP)
- Ohio Skilled Workforce Advancement Program (OSWAP)
- Community Assistance and Social Services Impact (CASSI) Loan Forgiveness Program
- CarbonSmart
- Public Funds, Public Trust Data Protection Act

These are policy/program design concepts unless a page explicitly states otherwise; do not describe them as enacted law or operating government programs.

### 05. Essays & public writing

Question: How can complex systems, cultural patterns, and emerging ideas be translated into accessible public argument?

Writing index:
https://leahbuzek.com/writing

This section includes cultural analysis, essays, field notes, and ideas that may later become more formal frameworks.

## Important lineage between works

- Calling It What It Is → TRACEs
  The research commentary names caregiver trauma; TRACEs develops the assessment and practice infrastructure that follows from that argument.

- Continuity of the Subjective Experience → Continuity Ethics → Relational Ontometry / RPCM → Promirational Ethics
  These works form a developing relational-ethics sequence. They should be read as related but non-identical layers: foundational argument, ethical framework, structural model, applied analytical model, and practice-oriented extension.

- EPIC ↔ Survivor Voices Council
  EPIC provides a general participatory-design framework for ethical collaboration with Experts by Experience; the Survivor Voices Council is an applied survivor-governance structure.

- Raise the Bar ↔ Nightlife Venues as Partners
  Raise the Bar is the applied campaign; Nightlife Venues as Partners addresses deliberative and institutional tensions around that strategy.

- IncuBrighter ↔ TRACEs / civic-capacity work
  IncuBrighter functions as an organizational home for developing research, pilots, tools, and early-stage community programs.

## Core themes

- care as infrastructure rather than sentiment
- relational ethics and mutual subjectivity
- power, proximity, recognition, and asymmetry
- caregiver trauma and child-to-parent violence
- survivor-centered and lived-experience-led systems design
- Experts by Experience and participatory governance
- public-service ethics
- civic capacity and grassroots infrastructure
- rural and underserved-community design
- policy mechanisms and implementation systems
- translation of complex ideas into usable structures
